questions.q: What does the editorial name as the reason for the unhappiness found among rich and poor alike?
options: People compare themselves with others
Not quite. The article says: Man seeks an explanation of life, and the world seems unexplained until the Hereafter is taken into account.
Man seeks an explanation of life, and the world seems unexplained until the Hereafter is taken into account
Yes. The answer he found was in the remembrance of God.
Wealth is unfairly shared
Not quite. The article says: Man seeks an explanation of life, and the world seems unexplained until the Hereafter is taken into account.
Modern life moves too fast
Not quite. The article says: Man seeks an explanation of life, and the world seems unexplained until the Hereafter is taken into account.
questions.rationale: “Man is born with an ‘explanation-seeking’ nature, but is compelled to live in a world that appears unexplained to him… the world Hereafter has to be taken into consideration.”

questions.q: The editorial compares life to a train journey towards a known destination. What is the point of the comparison?
options: One who is on the right path is glad at each stage, knowing he is nearer the goal of Paradise
Right. Death becomes a gateway, not an end.
Life passes too quickly to enjoy
Not quite. The article says: One who is on the right path is glad at each stage, knowing he is nearer the goal of Paradise.
Fellow travellers cannot be chosen
Not quite. The article says: One who is on the right path is glad at each stage, knowing he is nearer the goal of Paradise.
One should get down at every station
Not quite. The article says: One who is on the right path is glad at each stage, knowing he is nearer the goal of Paradise.
questions.rationale: “If you are on the right path… you will only be happy that every day and night you are coming closer to your goal which is none other than eternal Paradise.”

questions.q: How, according to the article, can militancy carried out in the name of religion be ended?
options: By stricter punishment alone
Not quite. The article says: By a counter-ideology – patiently showing the peaceful teaching of Islam – not by the gun.
By a counter-ideology – patiently showing the peaceful teaching of Islam – not by the gun
Yes. It is “ideology versus ideology.”
By closing schools of religion
Not quite. The article says: By a counter-ideology – patiently showing the peaceful teaching of Islam – not by the gun.
By ignoring it until it fades
Not quite. The article says: By a counter-ideology – patiently showing the peaceful teaching of Islam – not by the gun.
questions.rationale: “Modern Muslim militancy can be eradicated only by providing a counter-ideology… We should present to them the true ideology of Islam based on peace and tolerance.”

questions.q: The Quran promises those who are patient a reward “without measure.” How does the article understand this reward?
options: As victory over one’s enemies
Not quite. The article says: As the growth of one’s personality, which patience makes possible.
As the growth of one’s personality, which patience makes possible
Well read. Patience keeps anger and hatred from blocking natural growth.
As wealth in this world
Not quite. The article says: As the growth of one’s personality, which patience makes possible.
As a long life
Not quite. The article says: As the growth of one’s personality, which patience makes possible.
questions.rationale: “In the above verse of the Quran, reward refers to personality development… the biggest source of personality development is patience.”

questions.q: What simple method does the article recommend when one is upset by an unwanted situation?
options: Leave the place for a day
Not quite. The article says: Keep silent and empty the mind for thirty seconds.
Keep silent and empty the mind for thirty seconds
Correct. The wave of reaction breaks and passes.
Speak at once and clear the air
Not quite. The article says: Keep silent and empty the mind for thirty seconds.
Write down the complaint
Not quite. The article says: Keep silent and empty the mind for thirty seconds.
questions.rationale: “You need to empty your mind for thirty seconds by observing silence. As a result, the anti-wave that had arisen would break and disperse.”

questions.q: Pelé’s first football was a sock stuffed with rags. How does the article read his poverty?
options: As something he never spoke about
Not quite. The article says: As a challenge that awakened his drive – a blessing in disguise.
As a challenge that awakened his drive – a blessing in disguise
Yes. “Poverty is not deprivation. Rather, it is a challenge.”
As proof that talent needs money
Not quite. The article says: As a challenge that awakened his drive – a blessing in disguise.
As a curse he escaped by luck
Not quite. The article says: As a challenge that awakened his drive – a blessing in disguise.
questions.rationale: “Deprivation is a great motivator for achievement. One’s inner reservoir has a huge amount of energy which can compensate every kind of disadvantage.”

questions.q: In Quran 2:62 the Muslims are named together with Jews, Christians and Sabaeans. What does the article conclude?
options: The verse applies only to ancient times
Not quite. The article says: No community has a special claim; reward depends on true belief and righteous deeds.
No community has a special claim; reward depends on true belief and righteous deeds
Right. God regards a person’s thoughts and actions.
The order of the names shows their rank
Not quite. The article says: No community has a special claim; reward depends on true belief and righteous deeds.
All four communities are certain of salvation
Not quite. The article says: No community has a special claim; reward depends on true belief and righteous deeds.
questions.rationale: “Belonging to a particular community gives no special status in the eyes of God… people will be judged according to their deeds and character.”

questions.q: What contrast does the article lament?
options: People praise the dead and neglect the living
Not quite. The article says: People speak warmly and at length of a son, an ancestor or a hero, yet have nothing to say of God.
People know other lands better than their own
Not quite. The article says: People speak warmly and at length of a son, an ancestor or a hero, yet have nothing to say of God.
People speak much and act little
Not quite. The article says: People speak warmly and at length of a son, an ancestor or a hero, yet have nothing to say of God.
People speak warmly and at length of a son, an ancestor or a hero, yet have nothing to say of God
Yes. It asks whether hearts have “withered of all faith.”
questions.rationale: “Alas! Those people who have volumes in praise of man, but not even a few words in praise of God.”

questions.article: A Phenomenon of the Body, Not of the Soul
questions.q: Drummer Rick Allen lost an arm and returned to perform. What does the article say this shows?
options: Music heals the body
Not quite. The article says: The inner energy of a person stays whole even when part of the body is lost.
Only exceptional people can overcome loss
Not quite. The article says: The inner energy of a person stays whole even when part of the body is lost.
The inner energy of a person stays whole even when part of the body is lost
Exactly. It calls this a law of nature, open to all.
Modern medicine can replace any limb
Not quite. The article says: The inner energy of a person stays whole even when part of the body is lost.
questions.rationale: “If a person’s hand or leg is cut off, his inner energy still remains intact—it does not get diminished.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, does the pursuit of material enjoyment end in boredom while intellectual and spiritual pursuit does not?
options: The material domain is very limited, whereas the domain of thought and spirit has no boundary
Well reasoned. Newton felt like a boy on the shore of a vast ocean.
Boredom is a sign of illness
Not quite. The article says: The material domain is very limited, whereas the domain of thought and spirit has no boundary.
Material things cost too much
Not quite. The article says: The material domain is very limited, whereas the domain of thought and spirit has no boundary.
Spiritual people need less sleep
Not quite. The article says: The material domain is very limited, whereas the domain of thought and spirit has no boundary.
questions.rationale: “The domain of fulfilment in the material world is very limited; while, the domain of spiritual or intellectual fulfilment is so vast that words fail to express its endless boundaries.”
